cards.text: Friend, the writer of Hebrews is writing to believers in Jesus (Hebrews 3:1), and he's in the middle of a list of people who lived by faith. Again and again, he starts with the same two words: by faith. Now he comes back to Abraham, Israel's forefather, on the day Abraham was tested.

cards.question: When he was tested, Abraham was ready to offer up his one and only ___ on the altar.

cards.text: Here's the twist: God had already told him, “Through Isaac your offspring will be reckoned.” The promise runs through Isaac, and Isaac is the son on the altar.

cards.question: The promise says Isaac, and the test says Isaac. How does Abraham hold those two together?

answers.text: He reasoned that God could raise the dead
He figured God would change His mind
He decided the promise meant someone else

cards.question: The writer says that in a sense, Abraham did receive Isaac back from death.

cards.text: Then the list moves down the family line, and by faith Isaac blesses his sons Jacob and Esau concerning the future. When Jacob is dying, he blesses each of the sons of Joseph, his son.

cards.question: As dying Jacob leans on the top of his staff, what does he do?

cards.text: Next is Joseph, and his end is near. By faith he looks ahead, the way Isaac did when he blessed his sons.

cards.question: With his end near, what does Joseph speak about?

answers.text: A new king rising in Egypt

cards.text: Joseph also gives instructions about his bones.
Next is Moses, Israel's leader, and his part starts right after he's born. By faith his parents hide him for three months, because they saw that he was a beautiful child.

cards.question: Moses' parents were afraid of the king's edict.

cards.text: Years pass, and Moses is grown. By faith he refuses to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter, the daughter of Egypt's king.

cards.question: Moses chose the fleeting enjoyment of sin over suffering with God's people.

cards.text: Moses valued disgrace for Christ above the treasures of Egypt. Friend, people stay at a job they can't stand just for the parking spot, and this man puts the TREASURES OF EGYPT second.

cards.question: Moses valued disgrace for Christ above Egypt's treasures, because he was looking ahead to his ___.

cards.text: Moses isn't done yet: by faith he leaves Egypt, not afraid of the king's anger. Friend, I flinch when my oven timer goes off.

cards.question: Moses left Egypt without fearing the king's anger. What kept him going?

answers.text: He saw Him who is invisible
His brother Aaron went with him

cards.text: Then comes the Passover. By faith Moses keeps the Passover and the sprinkling of blood, and the destroyer of the firstborn is on the way.

cards.question: The Passover and the sprinkling of blood kept the destroyer from touching Israel's own firstborn.

cards.text: Now all the people step out in faith, right up to the Red Sea. Water in front, Egyptians behind. Friend, if my day started like that, I'd hit snooze until next week.

cards.question: By faith the people passed through the Red Sea as on ___ land.
The people crossed by faith. When the Egyptians tried to follow, they made it through the Red Sea too.

cards.text: Fast forward to Jericho, where by faith the walls fall, and the people's part takes seven days. SEVEN DAYS, friend, and I'm out of breath after stirring one batch of dough.

cards.question: Before the walls of Jericho fell, what did the people do to them for seven days?

cards.text: Next on the list is Rahab, the prostitute. By faith she does not perish with those who were disobedient.

cards.question: When Israel's spies came, what did Rahab do that kept her from perishing with the disobedient?

answers.text: She reported them to the king
She kept them out of the city

cards.text: Then the writer says, “And what more shall I say?” He's got way more people of faith than he can cover.

cards.question: The writer has plenty more people of faith, but he says ___ will not allow him to tell of them.

cards.text: So he rattles off names like somebody squeezing a whole week into a voicemail before it BEEPS. Gideon, Barak, Samson and Jephthah from the days of the judges, plus David, Israel's king, Samuel the prophet, and the prophets.
And here's what they did through faith: they conquered kingdoms, administered justice and gained what was promised.

cards.question: Some of these people of faith came face to face with lions. What does the writer say they did?

answers.text: They shut the mouths of lions
They chased lions out of the land
They hunted lions for the king

cards.question: Through faith they quenched the raging ___ and escaped the edge of the sword.
Through faith, some of these people gained strength from weakness.

cards.text: They became mighty in battle and put foreign armies to flight. Women even received back their dead, raised to life again.
Then the list takes a hard turn. Others were tortured and refused their release.

cards.question: Why did some people of faith refuse their release while being tortured?

answers.text: So they might gain a better resurrection
So their families would be spared
So the king would change his mind

cards.text: Still others endured mocking and flogging, and even chains and imprisonment. They were stoned, sawed in two and put to death by the sword.
They went around in sheepskins and goatskins, destitute, oppressed and mistreated. They wandered in deserts and mountains, and hid in caves and holes in the ground.

cards.question: After all these people went through, the writer says they were not worthy of the world.

cards.text: Looking back over the whole list, the writer says these were all commended for their faith, yet they did not receive what was promised. But that's not the end of it, because God had something planned.

cards.question: The people on this list did not receive what was promised. What does the writer say God had planned?
Because of God's plan, the people on this list would be made ___ together with us.
